normative_summary: Rendering owns Evaluation, RenderDSL, RenderDocument, and Renderer Command.
Only the authoritative server Evaluator and sealer may produce an Engine-admissible RenderDocument.
Web and client feedback is non-authoritative and cannot submit documents or digests, bypass admission, or call Engine.
No formal MaterializedScene, MaterializedTree, or second static language exists between DesignDSL and RenderDocument.
A request builder is private, transient, nonpersistent, noncacheable, nonpublic, and identityless.
Only one immutable RenderDocument is sealed after complete success.
RenderDocument is a request-scoped Renderer-only handoff, not an Artifact, Workspace item, audit object, or download.
Public Render or Preview returns only a RenderOutput description or structured problem.
Future static-document export requires a new contract without leases and internal identities.
v1 never caches or reuses RenderDocument across requests or caches RenderOutput across requests.
Every successful Evaluation enters Engine.
A future cache cannot skip current admission, capability demand, or Asset current selection.
Evaluation stages are a strict total order and any failed stage blocks every later stage.
Stage one authenticates and admits scope, strict request envelope, and outer capacity.
Stage two resolves root current and integrity-gates every candidate before reading TemplateRefs and freezing closure.
Stage three revalidates every unique snapshot semantics, scope, DAG, dependencies, profiles, and lowering edge.
Stage four validates RootDocument and constructs closed typed context and root Customs.
Stage five admits authored then external-public Asset atoms in canonical occurrence order.
Stage six gathers closure capability contracts and linearizes required CapabilityState.
Stage seven creates the root frame, lazily materializes, binds, and expands, and serially resolves Assets at consumers.
Stage eight seals the tree and manifest and forms capability, asset, result, and document digests.
Stage nine constructs the Renderer Command and invokes Engine.
Any root or child current drift discards the entire closure attempt and retries from the root only.
Closure cannot patch-read a child or mix temporal snapshots.
Frozen retry exhaustion returns TEMPLATE_CLOSURE_UNSTABLE.
After freeze, Template current is never reread; Asset current remains per-occurrence linearized.
Every Render distrusts readiness and current report and rechecks each snapshot under its permanent exact Profile.
Lost support for an admitted Profile is an internal compatibility breach, not an automatic INVALID mutation.
Persisted DesignDSL is re-canonicalized and contentHash-checked before snapshot creation.
A hash mismatch creates no snapshot, historical rewrite, or Evaluator payload.
Closure, dependency, input, and Asset admission collect bounded problems in their own fixed canonical order.
At the shared cap append PROBLEM_LIMIT_REACHED, stop the current stage, and never enter the next.
Unsafe malformed, hash, or Profile failures stop after one problem.
After state creation, the first demanded ValueSource, Definition, Binding, Capability, property, Asset, or capacity error terminates Evaluation.
A runtime error triggers no later Capability, Resolver, or lowering and no partial document.
Product semantics are one deterministic serial trace.
Parallel preparation is allowed only when demand, budget, error, selection, manifest, and tree observables remain serial-equivalent.
Thread completion order has no semantic effect.
A Definition lazily memoizes success or failure within its exact lexical frame.
One logical position is evaluated once.
A runtime failure affects the request only, not readiness, revision, or projection.
Ordinary Node consumer order is render, placement, visible, opacity, transform, kind properties, and children DFS.
Canvas order is root geometry and bleed, background, and children DFS.
Composite, Run, Point, Command, and Track values consume in catalog order.
JSON member, binding array, or bindingId order cannot change runtime order.
Repeat, Conditional, and TemplateUse use their frozen specialized orders.
render:false, false Conditional, zero Repeat, and SKIP prune before later binding, descendant, capability, and Asset work.
visible:false and opacity:0 do not prune and retain evaluation, resource, and layout failures.
Evaluator builds the complete typed static property tree and expands semantic defaults.
Evaluator preserves proof of author-materialized leaves.
Binding overlays only existing author-materialized targets allowed by Policy.
Default expansion cannot create a bindable target.
Post-overlay revalidates leaf, composite, placement, and Node aggregate.
ABSENT, error, type, or validation failure never falls back to baseline.
A Node resolves Assets only after all concrete properties pass post-binding validation.
Asset occurrences resolve serially in property and Run order before child DFS.
A Node validation failure signs no Asset lease.
True Conditional lowers to an appearance-free frame; Repeat containers and items lower to stack or grid and PACK placement.
Synthetic role stays sidecar-only and RenderDocument has no synthetic marker.
Post-binding semantics validate in authored units with arbitrary precision before lowering.
Lowering computes exact pt equal to mm times 360 divided by 127.
pt, unitless, and degree values quantize once to six decimals HALF_EVEN and normalize negative zero.
Actual RenderDSL values are rechecked for ranges, sign, min and max, finiteness, and pre-layout aggregates.
Quantization never repairs an authored error.
A quantization-caused zero, overflow, or contract failure terminates Evaluation.
Engine cannot redo semantic rounding or recompute from authored mm.
Evaluator rejects only contradictions knowable without layout.
The exact Layout Profile Engine uniquely determines final geometry and measure-dependent constraints.
Java cannot pre-layout, emit final geometry, text, glyph, or scene, or run a second layout algorithm.
A legal final-layout constraint failure is a request error and does not alter readiness.
An Engine-detected malformed, dynamic, or manifest residue is an internal RenderDocument breach.
Command, RenderDocument, and Layout Profile are three independent exact v1 contracts.
The new contracts claim no old Haibo compatibility and never silently downgrade.
RenderDocument is UTF-8 strict JSON rejecting duplicates, unknowns, null, and noncanonical scalars.
RenderDocument top level is the exact closed dslVersion, layoutProfile, canvas, and resources envelope.
The top level excludes request, deadline, output, business, Evaluation, and digest metadata.
Execution facts belong only in Command or Rendering internals.
The static Node kind union is exactly the frozen list.
Canvas is root-only and compositionViewport is lowering-only.
Repeat, Conditional, and TemplateUse are illegal in RenderDSL.
Every kind is a closed lowerCamel discriminator union without a generic property bag.
The versioned RenderNodeContractCatalog explicitly defines each approved lowering edge.
Lowering allows only frozen unit, resource, authored-field, structure, and default transformations.
Java sealer and Rust parser consume the same machine contract and corpus, not handwritten drifting switches.
Root Canvas and other Node closed fields are exactly frozen.
All defaults expand and authored-only IDs, display, bindings, and render are removed.
RenderDSL Placement is the closed ABSOLUTE, STACK, and GRID union with frozen rules and pt fields.
PACK must disappear during lowering.
compositionViewport permanently implies CONTAIN, CENTER, and source and host clipping.
compositionViewport sourceCanvas has exact closed fields and no bleed.
Viewport and sourceCanvas occurrences map to the use host and child Canvas background.
Seal assigns continuous uint64 preorder ordinals to every final real, synthetic, and sourceCanvas Node.
occurrenceId wire is rwocc_ plus 16 zero-padded lowercase hexadecimal digits.
Viewport traversal visits sourceCanvas before its children; pruned content has no ordinal.
visible:false, opacity:0, and empty Nodes retain ordinals.
Engine sees only opaque occurrenceId.
Author and resource backreferences exist only in the bounded request sidecar.
The sidecar is destroyed and excluded from document, identity, cache, log, and history.
Image and each Text Run require their respective resourceId field.
Nodes inline no URL, descriptor, or resource object.
Each actual resource property uses a unique resourceId even for identical content.
resources preserve resolve encounter order and exact Ticket13 closed fields.
The manifest excludes Asset, content, scope, and Template identities.
Tree references and manifest entries are an exact one-to-one bijection.
Missing, unused, duplicate, collision, kind, or count mismatch fails seal; no merge or prefetch residue remains.
DOCUMENT_SEAL begins only after Evaluation and Asset resolution succeed.
Precommit seal validates root, kinds, content, defaults, numbers, ordinals, manifest, resources, leases, and identity residue.
A capped counting writer validates only RenderDocument-owned capacities before commit.
Canonical bytes and digest commit atomically only after all checks pass.
Grapheme, glyph, line, paint, and clip budgets belong to Engine, not document seal.
Seal-discovered Evaluator structural residue is an internal lowering breach.
An ordinary runtime or capacity failure returns its domain code before atomic commit.
Document capacity specifically returns RENDER_DOCUMENT_LIMIT_EXCEEDED.
No preseal builder or canonical prefix reaches Engine.
An empty Canvas is valid and outputs its explicit background or transparent surface.
An empty Canvas inserts no placeholder.
Any preseal failure discards the builder, unsealed bytes, and sidecar and never calls Engine.
Committed state and Resolver records remain only to fixed expiry for unknown-commit safety.
Failure records are not resampled, deleted, or renewed and form no partial digest, document, or history.
Only allowed aggregate counts, stable code, and timing remain.
The Render canonical Profile fixes UTF-8 member ordering, Design string rules, shortest integers, and six-decimal plain numbers.
Canonical decimal forbids exponent, plus, trailing zero, negative zero, and nonfinite values.
All semantic arrays preserve frozen order and never set-sort.
The canonical writer never repairs, guesses, or deletes invalid values.
renderDocumentDigest uses frozen domain-separated SHA-256 over complete canonical bytes including lease URL and expiry.
The Command carries the digest and Engine verifies it.
Document digest is transport integrity only and excluded from identity, cache, log, public response, and persistence.
The same active request with the same frozen inputs, state, selections, and leases rebuilds a byte-identical document and digest.
A new request may differ because a new lease changes bytes.
Identity objects reuse frozen Design primitive canonical rules without metadata normalization or set inference.
Only explicitly named arrays sort; all others retain semantic order and objects are closed and nonnull.
closureDigest uses frozen domain-separated SHA-256 over the exact closure manifest.
The closure manifest binds scope and root, sorted unique snapshot facts, and sorted authored-edge facts.
Unreachable edges remain and a diamond snapshot appears once.
Readiness, display, and database row facts are excluded from closure digest.
admittedInputDigest hashes the exact closed typed schema, root, and custom input object.
Root includes only declared PRESENT fields, customs sort by definitionId, and ordinary arrays retain order.
Value contracts determine canonical wire without redundant type tags.
ABSENT, unknown, loser, private, raw lexical, order, and proof facts are excluded.
evaluationFingerprint hashes the exact closed scope, authorization, closure, input, contract, and budget object.
Authorization digest binds subject and decisions without a raw token.
Contract lists sort canonically and budget contains the full effective vector.
renderRequestId is a recovery record key only and is excluded from the fingerprint.
State, results, Asset current, lease, output, deadline, and timing are excluded from the fingerprint.
The fingerprint is for same-request recovery and conflict only and is never public or logged.
All identity hashes use sha256 plus 64 lowercase hexadecimal digits.
evaluationResultDigest exists only after successful document seal.
The result digest hashes the exact scope, closure, input, contract, capability, and Asset result object.
Subject, request, budget, lease, document digest, and output parameters are excluded.
The five request, fingerprint, result, document, and content identities are noninterchangeable.
A future output cache requires a completed result digest plus exact Renderer and Output Profiles and independent authorization and scope partition.
Renderer Command closed fields are exactly frozen.
One Command outputs exactly one complete root Canvas PNG or JPEG.
PNG and JPEG output objects and 96 and 90 defaults are exact and expanded before Command construction.
Command, document, Layout, Renderer, and Output Profiles are independently exact.
The Command contains no Template, Evaluation, Capability, or Asset business identity.
Canonical Command and domain-separated digest uniquely define same-request join, replay, conflict, and cancel.
An unknown transport result may resend only the same request and canonical Command before deadline with valid leases.
Retry cannot reseal, renew, resolve current, rebuild state, or extend the deadline.
A lost registry fails; a new request repeats the full Evaluation.
Engine validates authorization, Command, Profile, registry, document, and digest before resources or layout.
Engine cannot read the original Render request, Template current, DesignDSL, or sidecar.
Cancel, registry, seal, and transient outcome never change Evaluation identity.
Capacity axes cover all frozen closure, admission, runtime, resource, document, and diagnostic dimensions.
Grapheme, glyph, line, paint, clip, and raster counts are Engine-owned, not preseal document fields.
Dynamic capacity reserves atomically before frame, Node, resource, allocation, or external call.
An excess fails immediately without truncation or skipping.
One logical position counts once per Evaluation.
A retry consumes separate attempt, physical, and deadline budget without resetting semantic totals.
Only a new renderRequestId starts fresh budgets.
A statically provable excess fails before CapabilityState.
A dynamic excess returns the owner code with zero RenderDocument.
OOM, scheduler behavior, or downstream defaults cannot substitute for contract limits.
Public problem stage is one of the nine frozen closed stages.
The capacity catalog contains the nine frozen domain capacity codes and reuses more specific existing codes.
Encoding and geometry use their distinct non-capacity codes.
Specific domain errors never collapse to generic EVALUATION_FAILED.
An internal hash, Profile, document, or manifest breach publicly folds to RENDER_INTERNAL_ERROR plus a redacted operations alert.
A public problem has the exact {code,stage,safeLocation,parameters} base shape.
Capacity parameters expose only closed limitId, not actual, input, or omitted data.
Every limit oracle freezes code, stage, reservation, and zero-write, zero-document, and zero-output boundaries.
An admission locator may expose an authorized Template, revision, and canonical pointer.
Runtime or Engine initially exposes only opaque occurrence, resource, and safe property identity.
Sidecar author projection requires corresponding Template read and segment authorization.
An unreadable child segment is redacted; Asset identity additionally follows asset.read.
Problems, logs, traces, and metrics prohibit business, content, input, result, Asset, child, stack, and provider raw data.
Metrics labels are limited to bounded stage, code, Profile, and status.
Java Evaluator and sealer and Rust parser and validator independently replay the shared seam corpus before implementation readiness.
The shared corpus covers all listed structure, ordering, binding, quantization, manifest, residue, malformed, geometry, and breach classifications.
The Java authority and independent TypeScript implementation replay authoring Design, Input, and Expression vectors.
Executors need not replay semantics outside their seam.
The machine-readable RenderNodeContract and byte vectors are cross-language authority.
Same-named classes, screenshots, legacy scenes, or one-sided unit tests cannot substitute for the authority.

v1 excludes all listed formal IR, partial or streamed documents, prelayout, resume, reuse, public upload or download, storage, loose wire, plugin, fallback, callback, skip, placeholder, default-font, and partial-output features.
Ticket15 creates no product model, client, API, storage, cache, Engine adapter, or placeholder implementation.
